name: Scaling up training and making it more efficient
gist: These papers study how model performance improves as they get bigger and develop better training recipes using scaling laws, advanced optimization, and novel pretraining approaches.
explain: A striking pattern in machine learning is that bigger models trained on more data perform better on almost every task, which means size correlates with ability. This is called scaling, and the relationship is surprisingly predictable—if you know how well a small model performs, you can forecast how well a large one will, because the improvement follows a pattern. Papers in this area study the rules of scaling: how performance improves with model size, data size, and compute budget. They also study scaling laws—mathematical relationships that describe these patterns—so that researchers can plan experiments ahead of time and predict whether training a larger model is worth the cost, which saves wasted spending on experiments that will not work.

The deeper question is efficiency: how to get the most performance for a fixed budget of computation, which is the real constraint in research. A naive approach is just to make everything bigger, but that is wasteful because you spend money on techniques that do not help. Better approaches involve advanced optimization techniques, like adding noise to the direction-of-change calculations to escape getting stuck in local traps (dead ends in the search space where the model stops improving because it got stuck), or adjusting how fast the model learns to be quick early and careful later, so the model finds good solutions faster. Some papers also study new pretraining approaches, where instead of just predicting the next word, models are trained on other tasks that force them to learn deeper patterns, which teaches them richer representations upfront. The tricky part is that small experiments do not always predict what happens at scale—a technique that works in a small experiment might fail on a large model, or vice versa, because scaling changes what matters.

Understanding scaling matters because it determines whether companies can build bigger models and whether research labs with limited budgets can compete, which affects who gets to build new models. Papers that discover inefficiencies in training can make the process cheaper, which means more teams can afford to build models. Papers that characterize scaling laws help researchers decide which ideas are worth pursuing by predicting what works before you spend money testing it, which prevents wasted experiments. This area touches everything else: if you understand how to scale efficiently, you can afford to train larger models on better data, which helps you solve harder problems and study new techniques because you save money, so scaling efficiency unlocks everything downstream.

papers.title: Break the Trade-off Between Watermark Strength and Speculative Sampling Efficiency for Language Models
papers.contribution: Breaks the watermark-efficiency trade-off, improving detectability without sacrificing speculative sampling efficiency.

papers.title: Capacity-Aware Mixture Law Enables Efficient LLM Data Optimization
papers.contribution: Reduce mixture optimization costs by 50% while improving downstream benchmark performance by up to 3% when applied to Mixture-of-Experts models up to 55B-A1.2B parameters.

papers.title: How to Train Your Advisor: Steering Black-Box LLMs with Advisor Models
papers.contribution: Advisor Models improve GPT-5.2 on RuleArena (Taxes) by 27.4%, reduce Gemini 3 Pro SWE agent steps by 24.6%, outperform static prompt optimizers in personalization, and transfer to stronger models.

papers.title: KnowledgeSmith: Uncovering Knowledge Updating in LLMs with Model Editing and Unlearning
papers.contribution: Results show LLMs do not exhibit similar updating as humans for different knowledge levels, and there exists consistency-capacity trade-off between editing reliability and model performance.

papers.title: NI Sampling: Accelerating Discrete Diffusion Sampling by Token Order Optimization
papers.contribution: NI Sampling achieves up to 14.3x acceleration over full-step sampling with negligible performance drop, consistently outperforming confidence threshold baselines.

papers.title: Optimal Sparsity of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models for Reasoning Tasks
papers.contribution: Identifies Active FLOPs and Total tokens per parameter as joint determinants of optimal sparsity: reasoning benefits from optimal TPP while memorization improves with more parameters.

papers.title: Predicting Large Model Test Losses with a Noisy Quadratic System
papers.contribution: Enables finding optimal model configuration, batch size, and update count under explicit resource constraints with model-selected configurations close to ground-truth optimal.

papers.title: Swordsman: Entropy-Driven Adaptive Block Partition for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art performance via training-free adaptive partitioning and dynamic threshold adjustment for improved efficiency and stability.

papers.title: Teaching Metric Distance to Discrete Autoregressive Language Models
papers.contribution: Consistent gains in visual grounding, robotic manipulation, and image generation, with strongest improvements in low-data regimes.

papers.title: The Labyrinth and the Thread: Rethinking Regularizations in Sequential Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: The framework simplifies sequential knowledge editing, eliminates unnecessary regularization strategies, and robustly handles conflicting edits while maintaining consistent behavior.

papers.title: Towards Greater Leverage: Scaling Laws for Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
papers.contribution: Scaling laws accurately predict MoE efficiency based on configuration; MoE-mini (0.85B active) matches 6.1B dense model while using 7x fewer computational resources.

papers.title: $A_2$DEPT: Large Language Model–Driven Automated Algorithm Design via Evolutionary Program Trees
papers.contribution: A2DEPT consistently outperforms baselines across benchmarks, reducing optimality gap by an average of 9.8%.

papers.title: AC-ODM: Actor–Critic Online Data Mixing for Sample-Efficient LLM Pretraining
papers.contribution: AC-ODM reaches optimal validation perplexity on Pythia-1B with 66% fewer training steps and achieves 27.5% improvement in MMLU accuracy with negligible overhead.

papers.title: ADEPT: Continual Pretraining via Adaptive Expansion and Dynamic Decoupled Tuning
papers.contribution: The method outperforms full-parameter continual pretraining by up to 5.76% on general benchmarks while tuning only 15% of parameters and reducing training time by nearly 50%.

papers.title: Advantage Collapse in Group Relative Policy Optimization: Diagnosis and Mitigation
papers.contribution: AVSPO reduces advantage collapse by 58-63% relative to GRPO and yields consistent accuracy gains of 4-6 percentage points across model scales with improved generalization.

papers.title: Affine-Scaled Attention: Towards Flexible and Stable Transformer Attention
papers.contribution: Large-scale LLM pretraining experiments show consistent improvements in training stability, optimization behavior, and downstream task performance compared to standard softmax attention and attention sink baselines.

papers.title: AgentVocab: Structure-Aware Vocabulary Adaptation for Efficient LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Preserves tool-calling performance while reducing latency by 17.7% and 19.5% on τ-bench and τ²-bench respectively, with seamless integration into standard agent pipelines.

papers.title: Auto-regressive In-context Demonstration Selection
papers.contribution: AutoSelect outperforms existing heuristic and learning-based methods by up to 11% across nine datasets by optimizing over the factorial space of demonstration permutations via KL-regularized Plackett-Luce ranking.

papers.title: AutoSizer: Automatic Sizing of Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuits via Large Language Model (LLM) Agents
papers.contribution: Proposes AutoSizer achieving higher solution quality, faster convergence, and higher success rates than traditional optimization and LLM-based agents on AMS-SizingBench.

papers.title: BIOARC: Discovering Optimal Neural Architectures for Biological Foundation Models
papers.contribution: Identifies novel hybrid architectures up to 25x smaller than state-of-the-art models while maintaining superior performance and derives empirical design principles validated on biological data.

papers.title: BLISS: A Lightweight Bilevel Influence Scoring Method for Data Selection in Language Model Pretraining
papers.contribution: Achieves 1.7x speedup reaching same performance as state-of-the-art method on 1B setting while delivering superior downstream performance on 410M/1B/2.8B models.

papers.title: Beyond Drift: Stabilizing Subjective LLM Evaluation with Information-Theoretic Rubrics
papers.contribution: EIG-based approach substantially improves evaluation consistency and alignment with human judgments on six benchmarks including CharacterEval and MT-Bench, outperforming CoT and fixed-questionnaire baselines.

papers.title: CLAA: Cross-Layer Attention Aggregation for Accelerating LLM Prefill
papers.contribution: Establishes that as few as 10% of prompt tokens suffice to match full-context performance, identifies layer instability in existing heuristics, and achieves improved token selection.

papers.title: Cactus: Accelerating Auto-Regressive Decoding with Constrained Acceptance Speculative Sampling
papers.contribution: Increases acceptance rates while guaranteeing controlled distribution divergence, improving decoding throughput across diverse benchmarks.

papers.title: Can Language Models Discover Scaling Laws?
papers.contribution: For the first time demonstrates that agents can automatically discover scaling laws that exhibit more accurate extrapolation than established human-derived counterparts across all tasks.

papers.title: Cite Pretrain: Retrieval-Free Knowledge Attribution for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Achieves citation accuracy of 95.2% with only 3.5% human involvement on CitePretrainBench, enabling retrieval-free knowledge attribution without test-time retrieval.

papers.title: CoFrGeNet: Continued Fraction Architectures for Language Generation
papers.contribution: CoFrGeNets achieve competitive or superior performance on classification, Q&A, reasoning, and text understanding tasks with two-thirds to half the parameters and shorter pretraining time than GPT2-xl and Llama3 models.

papers.title: Context-level Language Modeling by Learning Predictive Context Embeddings
papers.contribution: Demonstrates 39% parameter reduction to achieve baseline perplexity and robust downstream task improvements under equivalent parameter counts across GPT-2 and Pythia backbones.

papers.title: CrispEdit: Low-Curvature Projections for Scalable Non-Destructive LLM Editing
papers.contribution: High edit success with capability degradation below 1% on average, significantly improving over prior editors.

papers.title: D$^3$: Dynamic Directional Graph-Constrained Data Scheduling for LLM Training
papers.contribution: Consistent improvements over existing data scheduling methods on pre-training and post-training phases with scalable approximation algorithms.

papers.title: Demystifying Entropy Control in LLM RL Training: Theoretical Analysis and Dynamic Scheduling
papers.contribution: Adaptive scheduling substantially improves Pass@K by 6.7% on AIME24 and 17.52% on puzzle tasks, consistently outperforming recent state-of-the-art reasoning methods.

papers.title: Do Not Let Low-Probability Tokens Over-Dominate in RL for LLMs
papers.contribution: The methods improve GRPO-trained LLM performance with up to 46.2% improvement on K&K Logic Puzzle reasoning tasks through more balanced token-level updates.

papers.title: Fast Data Mixture Optimization via Gradient Descent
papers.contribution: FastMix outperforms baselines while drastically reducing search cost: pre-training score 48.2 with 1.3 GPU-hours (×550 vs RegMix), post-training +5.5 gain.

papers.title: From Backward Spreading to Forward Replay: Revisiting Target Construction in LLM Parameter Editing
papers.contribution: Achieves same computational complexity while producing more accurate layer-wise targets; simple approach without interfering with initial target computation, broadly applicable to wide range of editing methods.

papers.title: GradMem: Learning to Write Context into Memory with Test-Time Gradient Descent
papers.contribution: The method outperforms forward-only memory writers with equal memory size and shows additional gradient steps scale capacity more effectively than repeated forwards on key-value retrieval and language tasks.

papers.title: Graph-Link: Bridging the Semantic-Structural Gap in Text-to-SQL via Constrained Subgraph Induction
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art schema linking with up to 7.0% improvement in recall/hit rates and 13.8% boost in SQL generation accuracy on complex queries on BIRD and Spider 2.0.

papers.title: ICPO: Provable and Practical In-Context Policy Optimization for Test-Time Scaling
papers.contribution: Minimum-Entropy ICPO achieves top-tier performance on mathematical reasoning while keeping inference costs affordable, providing principled understanding of self-reflection in LLMs.

papers.title: InfoDLM: an Information-Adaptive Framework for Discrete Diffusion Language Model Pretraining
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 13% improvement in reasoning accuracy over LLaDA variant under comparable pretraining budgets through adaptive masking.

papers.title: It's All Connected: A Journey Through Test-Time Memorization, Attentional Bias, Retention, and Online Optimization
papers.contribution: Different Miras designs yield models with varying strengths; instances outperform Transformers on language modeling, reasoning, recall, and time series tasks.

papers.title: Let's (not) just put things in Context: Test-time Training for Long-context LLMs
papers.contribution: Improves average accuracy by +12.6 on LongBench-v2 and +14.1 on ZeroSCROLLS; more efficient than thinking tokens for long contexts.

papers.title: MesaNet: Sequence Modeling by Locally Optimal Test-Time Training
papers.contribution: Optimal test-time training enables lower perplexity and higher benchmark performance than previous RNNs, especially on tasks requiring long context understanding.

papers.title: Meta Context Engineering via Agentic Skill Evolution
papers.contribution: Achieves 5.6-53.8% relative improvement over state-of-the-art agentic context engineering (mean 16.9%); maintains superior context adaptability, transferability, and efficiency.

papers.title: OMAC: A Holistic Optimization Framework for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.contribution: Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of OMAC on diverse tasks against recent approaches.

papers.title: Olmix: A Framework for Data Mixing Throughout LM Development
papers.contribution: Matches performance of full recomputation with 74% less compute after domain updates while improving downstream task performance by 11.6% over training without mixing.

papers.title: On Stable Long-Form Generation: Benchmarking and Mitigating Length Volatility
papers.contribution: SELB improves mean output length by 148% and reduces volatility by 69% without additional training.

papers.title: On the Limits of Test-Time Compute: Sequential Reward Filtering for Better Inference
papers.contribution: Demonstrates both theoretically and empirically that reward filtering provides tighter bounds than best-of-n, with consistent improvements across diverse benchmarks.

papers.title: Optimal Splitting of Language Models from Mixtures to Specialized Domains
papers.contribution: The approach consistently improves performance across common sense and reasoning benchmarks across different model sizes and compute budgets by optimally balancing general and specialized training.

papers.title: Optimizing Diversity and Quality through Base-Aligned Model Collaboration
papers.contribution: Achieve 21.3% joint improvement in diversity and quality within a single pass while maintaining strong controllability.

papers.title: ParEVO: Synthesizing Code for Irregular Data: High-Performance Parallelism through Agentic Evolution
papers.contribution: On the ParEval benchmark, ParEVO achieves 107x average speedup and 13.6x speedup on complex irregular graph problems, outperforming GPT-5-Thinking and Gemini-3-Pro while matching expert human-written baselines.

papers.title: Post-Training Language Models for Crosslingual Consistency
papers.contribution: Across 26 languages and diverse LLMs, DCO significantly improves crosslingual consistency and outperforms existing methods, enabling targeted alignment of low-resource languages.

papers.title: Pretrain Value, Not Reward: Decoupled Value Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: DVPO matches or surpasses state-of-the-art RLHF methods on MT-Bench, Alpaca-Eval, and Arena-Hard while reframing RLHF as policy optimization guided by a single pretrained value model.

papers.title: Pretraining Scaling Laws for Generative Evaluations of Language Models
papers.contribution: Identifies that generative evaluations introduce hyperparameters acting as control levers for scaling behavior, with the gold reference likelihood law uniquely stable across 5 orders.

papers.title: Principled RL for Diffusion LLMs Emerges from a Sequence-Level Perspective
papers.contribution: ESPO achieves 20-40 point improvements on mathematical reasoning tasks like Countdown while maintaining gains on math and coding benchmarks, establishing sequence-level optimization as principled for diffusion LLMs.

papers.title: RePro: Training Language Models to Faithfully Recycle the Web for Pretraining
papers.contribution: Delivers 3.7%-14.5% relative accuracy gains on downstream tasks by recycling 72B tokens from DCLM-RefinedWeb, improving organic data efficiency by 2-3× while doubling the performance gains of state-of-the-art web recycling.

papers.title: Reformulation for Pretraining Data Augmentation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates superior scaling properties up to 13B parameters against data repetition and upsampling baselines.

papers.title: Removing Noise, not Finding Gold: Quality Filtering for Large-Scale Pretraining
papers.contribution: CQF outperforms direct high-quality training because it filters low-quality data without harming high-quality, revealing mechanisms behind quality selection.

papers.title: Rewiring Experts on the Fly: Continuous Rerouting for Better Online Adaptation in Mixture-of-Expert Models
papers.contribution: The method achieves 5.5% improvement on HumanEval with OLMoE and 6% average gains when combined with self-consistency on DeepSeek-V2-Lite, maintaining robustness to context shifts.

papers.title: SAC-Opt: Semantic Anchors for Iterative Correction in Optimization Modeling
papers.contribution: Improves average modeling accuracy by 7.7% with gains up to 21.9% on ComplexLP, without requiring additional training or supervision.

papers.title: SIPDO: Closed-Loop Prompt Optimization via Synthetic Data Feedback
papers.contribution: This feedback-driven loop enables systematic improvement of prompt performance without assuming access to external supervision or new tasks.

papers.title: Sapiens2
papers.contribution: Sapiens2 sets new state-of-the-art across pose (+4 mAP), body-part segmentation (+22.3 mIoU), normal estimation (+29.2 rel-angular error) and extends to pointmap and albedo estimation.

papers.title: Scaling Laws Revisited: Modeling the Role of Data Quality in Language Model Pretraining
papers.contribution: Higher-quality data substantially reduces model size and compute requirements, with sublinear decay of effective data with quality and robustness to moderate corruption.

papers.title: Scaling Laws and Architectural Frontiers in Metagenomic Foundation Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates Llama architecture exhibits superior scaling efficiency and semantic retrieval; derives quality-aware power-law scaling laws for metagenomics.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Diffusion Transformers
papers.contribution: For the first time confirms scaling laws exist in DiT and accurately predicts text-to-image generation loss for a 1B model with 1.5e21 FLOPs compute budget.

papers.title: Scaling with Collapse: Efficient and Predictable Training of LLM Families
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that loss curve collapse emerges as a signature of compute-efficient training and enables practical early stopping benefits, proven on competitive LLM family Celerity.

papers.title: Scheduling Thoughts: Learning the Order of Thought in Diffusion Language Models
papers.contribution: Self-Aware Scheduling (SAS) improves Sudoku accuracy from 82.0% to 91.8% on 1B MDM and GSM8K pass@1 from 64% to 76%, consistently matching or exceeding heuristic schedules.

papers.title: Selective Deferred Routing: Enabling Cost-Efficient Collaboration between Local SLMs and Remote LLMs
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms existing multi-LLM collaboration methods across diverse models and datasets under various cost-performance trade-offs.

papers.title: Semantic Tube Prediction: Beating LLM Data Efficiency with JEPA
papers.contribution: Allows LLMs to match baseline accuracy with 16x less training data, directly violating data-efficiency bounds of scaling laws.

papers.title: Sharpness-Aware Pretraining Mitigates Catastrophic Forgetting
papers.contribution: Across 20M-150M models, flat-minima approaches reduce forgetting up to 80% after post-training, with SAM mid-training reducing forgetting 31% after MetaMath and 40% after quantization at scale.

papers.title: Synthetic Bootstrapped Pretraining
papers.contribution: Consistently improves upon baseline and delivers significant fraction of oracle improvement with 20x more unique data.

papers.title: TAMPO: Task- and Model-Aware Automatic Prompt Optimization for Auto-Routing in LLM-based Systems
papers.contribution: Achieves stable performance across 86 tasks and diverse models with flexible, cost-effective deployment for auto-routing in LLM-based systems.

papers.title: TextResNet: Decoupling and Routing Optimization Signals in Compound AI Systems via Deep Residual Tuning
papers.contribution: Achieves superior performance compared to TextGrad with remarkable stability on agentic tasks where baselines collapse.

papers.title: Towards Efficient LLMs Annealing with Principled Sample Selection
papers.contribution: Consistently achieves SOTA across model scales; identifies samples aligning with optimal curvature-aware descent path.

papers.title: Training–Inference Consistent Segmented Execution for Long-Context LLMs
papers.contribution: Achieves performance comparable to full-context attention with competitive latency-memory trade-offs and approximately 6x lower peak prefill memory at 128K context compared to full-context with FlashAttention.

papers.title: Tuning the Implicit Regularizer of Masked Diffusion Language Models: Enhancing Generalization via Insights from $k$-Parity
papers.contribution: Achieves 8.8% perplexity improvement on 50M-parameter models and 5.8% on 8B-parameter models across pre-training and fine-tuning.

papers.title: Tvcache: A Tool-Value Cache for Post-Training LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 70% cache hit rates and reduces median tool execution time by up to 6.9x with no degradation in post-training reward.

papers.title: Understanding Data Temporality Impact on Large Language Models Pre-training
papers.contribution: Sequentially trained models match shuffled baselines on general understanding while exhibiting more up-to-date and temporally precise knowledge; temporally ordered pretraining improves factual freshness.

papers.title: UniUGG: Unified 3D Understanding and Generation via Geometric-Semantic Encoding
papers.contribution: First unified framework for 3D understanding and generation supporting spatial VQA and 3D generation from reference images and arbitrary view transformations.

papers.title: Video2GUI: Synthesizing Large-Scale Interaction Trajectories for Generalized GUI Agent Pretraining
papers.contribution: Video2GUI constructs WildGUI with 12 million interaction trajectories spanning 1,500 applications; pre-training on it yields 5-20% improvements in GUI grounding and action benchmarks.

papers.title: Webscale-RL: Automated Data Pipeline for Scaling RL Data to Pretraining Levels
papers.contribution: Achieves performance of continual pretraining with 100x fewer tokens through more efficient RL training.

papers.title: When Data Is Scarce: Scaling Sparse Language Models with Repeated Training
papers.contribution: Results show sparse scaling laws for data-limited settings, demonstrate that sparsity postpones data saturation, and characterize resource trade-offs where loss-optimal sparsity is ~50% while compute-optimal sparsity is higher and scales with data.

papers.title: Why Attention Patterns Exist: A Unifying Temporal Perspective Analysis
papers.contribution: Framework explains distinct attention behaviors and when they emerge, enabling application to KV cache compression and LLM pruning with theoretically-inspired metrics.

papers.title: Words & Weights: Streamlining Multi-Turn Interactions via Co-Adaptation
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 37.8% accuracy improvement and reduces interaction turns by 40%, with proof that semantic pre-conditioning strictly reduces required parameter shift.

papers.title: ZIP-RC: Zero-overhead Inference-time Prediction of Reward and Cost for Adaptive and Interpretable Generation
papers.contribution: Enables zero-overhead inference-time adaptive sampling via utility-maximizing meta-actions on expected reward and compute tradeoffs.

papers.title: dTRPO : Trajectory Reduction in Policy Optimization of Diffusion Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Substantially improves core performance (up to 9.6% on STEM, 4.3% on coding) with efficient single-forward training.

papers.title: daVinci-Dev: Agent-native Mid-training for Software Engineering
papers.contribution: On SWE-Bench Verified, the 56.1% and 58.5% resolution rates for 32B and 72B models match or exceed prior open agentic recipes while using fewer mid-training tokens.

papers.title: mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
papers.contribution: mHC enables stable training at scale with tangible performance improvements and superior scalability compared to standard Hyper-Connections, supporting deeper understanding of topological architecture design.

papers.title: xLSTM Scaling Laws: Competitive Performance with Linear Time-Complexity
papers.contribution: xLSTM models consistently Pareto-dominate Transformers, delivering lower cross-entropy loss for the same compute budget with favorable scaling behavior.
